chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 19 of 21): the poet traces the body from the womb to the burning ground, sets kin and Death's rope against the feet, confesses the lure of women and calls himself every name of fault, and asks for steady wisdom, the yogic ascent to the thousand-petalled lotus, the company of devotees and release; one song is a love-lament and one a vow not to forget the feet even in lovemaking.
structure_note: Life-cycle songs: 1263 (Brahma shaping the body), 1265 (born, crawled, walked, became a corpse), 1270 (the body of filth and bone), 1272 (from conception to the harlot's net). Kin and Death: 1266 and 1267. Yoga: 1264 and 1275. Women: 1262, 1271, 1273, 1276. Self-reproach: 1269. Akam lament: 1268. 1274 asks to join the devotees, with a Krishna praise.

1262.reading: The poet describes lovemaking with women, hair loosening, breasts thrilled, the drinking of mouths and the nail-marks of passion on the bed, and asks whether he will forget that desire and know Murugan. The praise tells the Valli story at length: at Narada's word Murugan went seeking his lady in the millet field, lost his shame, changed his form in deceit, walked till his lotus feet ached, struck by Kama's arrows, up the hunters' hill, and married the girl born of the deer the great sage joined.
1262.nuance: The praise matches the confession: நாணம் அழிந்து, மார சரம்பட மோகமுடன், the god himself is shamed and struck by Kama for Valli. Line 274 lacks its beat marker and may have lost a word.

1263.reading: Before the waves of suffering of this body arise, the body that Brahma skilfully fashions with disease, deeds and troubles, a hut with hands and two legs into which life enters and which is sent into the world and ends in fire, the poet asks for a love for life that says 'Murugan who comes on the emerald peacock'. The praise names the vel that pierced the hill and dried the sea, the Tamil-mouthed one who gave sweet Tamil to Siva so the two deeds would leave, and the Lord who pities the poor more than those who sing with many arts.
1263.nuance: பிரமனும் விரகொடு பிணி வினை இடர் கொடு: Brahma builds the body out of disease and deeds themselves. இசை மொழிபவரினும் ஏழைக்கு இரங்கும்: the Lord prefers the helpless to the accomplished singers, a striking claim from a poet.

1264.reading: The poet asks whether, knowing the elements and kalas, rejoicing in yoga and worship and the way faults go, knowing the yogi's delight called Nada-Paraparam that came out of Bindu and the full and causal power, feeling the breath of wisdom and seeing the light, he will reach the two feet of the Lord seated on the lotus where a thousand nadis meet. The praise is a litany of the Goddess, Sarvesvari, Kali, Pidari, Vani, Varahi, Abhirami, Sivakami, Uma, sister of Vishnu, mother of the worlds, consort of the matted-haired dancer, who bore Murugan.
1264.nuance: நாடி ஒராயிரம் வந்த தாமரை is the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown, where the Lord's feet are to be reached. The sequence பூரணி காரணி விந்து வெளியான நாத பராபரம் sets Shakti, Bindu and Nada in the yogic order, and the praise turns entirely to the Goddess. How the opening (பூதகலாதிகள்) divides is uncertain.

1265.reading: The poet traces the body: they came in love, formed in the womb, were born, lay, sat, crawled, walked, weakened and became corpses, carried to the burning forest and burned; and he, worn out by this ruined body that falls when desire goes, asks Murugan to say 'fear not'. The praise tells of Rama going into the forest with his younger brother, crying 'where is my lady?', and of the monkey that burned Lanka, names Murugan his nephew, and Valli's partner whom the gods praise.
1265.nuance: பிறந்தார் கிடந்தார் இருந்தார் தவழ்ந்தார் நடந்தார் தளர்ந்து பிணமானார்: a life told as a list of verbs, in the plural of what others did. The plea asks only for reassurance (அஞ்சல்).

1266.reading: Before Death, the wicked punisher, throws his long rope and seizes his life while brothers born with him, kin and wife gather in the house quarrelling daily and his attachment to wealth grows, the poet asks to melt with devotion to the guru and be given words of Murugan's truth to speak of his feet. The praise names him the one whose victory in beautiful Tamil is praised beyond the directions, Valli's bridegroom who loves the sweetness of her words in the hut, the teacher who gave the three-eyed Siva the beginning of release, and the piercer of Krauncha.
1266.nuance: The household is pictured as a daily quarrel over property (நித்தப் பிணக்கிட்டு ... பொருட்பற்று). நிற் தத்துவச் சொற்கள்: the plea is for doctrine as speech. குருப் பத்தி may be devotion to Murugan as guru or to a human teacher.

1267.reading: Before Yama comes on his black buffalo seeking him and twists out his life, while the great illusory grief, deeper than the sea, for children, mothers, in-laws, wife and dependents withers him, the poet asks for a little of Murugan's lotus feet so that he may live with his mind stilled. The praise recalls Siva burning Kama with his third eye before the gods in yoga, and names Murugan the one who gave unattainable knowledge to Vishnu, who melts at the songs of devotees and is sweet to Devayanai and Valli.
1267.nuance: மாயத் துயரம்: the grief for kin is called illusory, and the list of relatives is the burden. சித்தம் ஓவித் துயிலும் அற்று: the stilling of mind and end of sleep is the life asked for. Who receives the 'knowledge beyond reach' (எட்டொணா வித்தை) is unclear.

1268.reading: In the voice of someone watching a love-sick girl, the singer says that the moon-faced creeper, wounded by Kama's fresh lotus arrow and the pearl-and-shell sea, frightened on her fragrant bed, her clothes and hair in disorder, is wasting away, and asks the lover to send his kura blossoms quickly. The praise names Murugan whose feet are worshipped by Brahma and Vishnu, Valli's bridegroom, dweller in the lotus of Saravana pool, who fought the asura armies.
1268.nuance: This is akam poetry, not the poet's confession; the speaker is likely the mother or friend. The request for the hero's flowers (குரவு அலர்) matches the garland asked for in 1254. புதனை in the praise is obscure.

1269.reading: The poet calls himself a chain of names, senseless sinner, angry man without a guru's path, ghost whose mind won't settle, coward who will not leave maya, idler who never thinks of penance, miser, one who shuns the assembly, wretch who will not leave the quarrel of deeds, and asks to be given the path of supreme wisdom to reflect on. The praise names the Kumara whose vel split Sura in two, who keeps sweet-spoken virtuous people from the womb and ever young, the guru of Siva who wears the river and serpent, and Valli's lover.
1269.nuance: The self-abuse is the song's whole first half: each epithet ends in a noun of contempt (பாவி, கோபி, பேயன், பேடி, மோடி, லோபி, கோழை, கூளன்). இனிய சொல் மறாத சீலர் கருவழி வராமல்: those who keep sweet speech are spared rebirth. மிகுமுனருபதானம் and நடைபெறு க்டுர are garbled.

1270.reading: Before the breath leaves this cage made of filth, skin, water and bone and father, wife, mother and kin cry out at the burning ground, the poet asks to become Murugan's servant who worships him. The praise names Murugan the great life who proclaims the sastras while Siva the dancer watches and praises, the vel that struck Sura in the sea, and the Lord who gives to those who guard dharma without sleeping.
1270.nuance: The song is set in doubled hard syllables (மலந்தோற் சலந்தேற் றெலும்பாற்), and the body as கூடு of filth and bone is clear while much else is a guess. Murugan teaching sastra with Siva as delighted listener repeats the teacher-of-Siva theme.

1271.reading: The poet confesses a mind that thinks a hundred crore sorrows in an instant, embracing in Kama's sulks, desire for women that deluded him and wasted his sense, and a body weakened by lust, and asks that on the day it falls Murugan come running on his peacock and give the house of open wisdom. The praise names him the Kumara who wandered the hunters' hills and bowed at the girl's feet, nephew of Vishnu who as Rama built the bridge and defeated Ravana, and the vel that crushed the demons who imprisoned sages and gods, leaving them to vultures.
1271.nuance: வெளி ஞான வீடு, the house of open (spacious) wisdom, is the release asked for. சிறுபேதை கால் பணிந்த: Murugan bowing at Valli's feet. விநன்முடி in line 3 is garbled.

1272.reading: The poet traces his life from conception in passion through the womb, the months and birth, to crawling, wearing jewels, walking, wandering as he pleased, smearing on stinking civet and mixing in the harlot's net, and asks whether he must die so. The praise tells of Vishnu splitting the crocodile when the elephant cried 'First one, refuge!', names his tortoise, fish, boar, dwarf and man-lion forms, and Siva as the column of light at Arunai, and ends with Murugan embracing Valli.
1272.nuance: The life comes full circle: it begins in மாதர் மயல் and ends in வேசி வலை. The images of gestation (தேனுகுடம் எனத் திரண்டு, a gathering like a honey pot) are hard to read exactly. The Gajendra story and the avatars are named outright.

1273.reading: The poet describes women whose pearl-hung breasts are like an elephant's tusks and whose spear eyes wound, so that his mind is clouded, his pure sense gone and he whirls in grief, and asks instead to worship the two feet with many words on his tongue and be given a little of the life of the lotus. The praise names Vishnu who in wrath felled the ten heads, Murugan's courtship of Valli, the meaning of the Veda that frees devotees from deeds, and the Lord praised by those learned in devotion and wisdom.
1273.nuance: சொற்கமல வாழ்வு may mean the life of the lotus feet won by words, or a 'lotus of speech'; the plea is again for praise as the way.

1274.reading: Calling Murugan peacock warrior, Saravana, lover immersed in Valli's breasts, and guru who taught old Siva the end of the bonds of Lord, soul and bond, melting, dancing, singing, seeking and wearing his feet, the poet asks whether a day will come when, with worldly desire gone, he joins Murugan's devotees through steady wisdom. The praise is a Krishna catalogue: the demoness's breast drunk, the elephant's tusks wrenched, the wood-apple demon struck, the bird, the twin marutha trees and the cart, the child reared in the cowherds' settlement, and names Murugan his nephew.
1274.nuance: பதி பசு பாசத் தீர்வினை: the Saiva Siddhanta triad of pati, pasu and pasa is the teaching Murugan gives Siva here. உணர்வினோடு ஊடிக் கூடியும், sulking and reuniting, brings the lover's quarrel into worship. The goal is the company of devotees, not release alone.

1275.reading: The poet asks for the light sought above the root centre in the forest of the mind's delusion, the state of silence, the secret instruction by which Murugan's play teaches a way not given in the many paths, and the steady, unfading gem-light in the middle channel. The praise names him Vishnu's nephew, guru to Siva the lord of the trident whose foot kicked Yama, and the light dancing to drum syllables.
1275.nuance: மூலா நிலமதின் மேலே and நடு வழி point to the muladhara and the central channel of yoga; வாடா மணி ஒளி is the light at its end. ரகசிய உபதேசம், secret instruction, makes Murugan the yogi's guru. நநடு doubles a syllable, and நாலா ருசி அமுது is obscure.

1276.reading: The poet describes lovemaking frankly, reddened eyes, sweat, ringing anklets, loosened hair, shaking breasts and bending waist, and says that even if he embraces women and his mind is deluded, he will not forget Murugan's shining feet. The praise recalls the churning of the sea when poison rose and the gods begged in fear, and Murugan on the great peacock that shook the heights and protected the world.
1276.nuance: மதிமயங்கினும் ... நின் பதங்கள் மறவேனே: unlike most songs, this one does not ask to be freed from women but vows remembrance in the midst of them.

links.note: The Naladiyar's 'he stood, he sat, he lay, and with kin wailing he was gone' urges virtue now; 1265 extends the same list of verbs from birth to corpse (பிறந்தார் கிடந்தார் இருந்தார் தவழ்ந்தார் நடந்தார்) and turns it into a plea for the Lord's 'fear not'.

The Naladiyar lists entrails, blood, bone, sinew and skin and asks where the woman is among them; 1270 calls the body a cage of filth, skin, water and bone, but draws service to the Lord from it rather than disgust at women.
Tirumular rouses the root and joins it to the head through the middle channel to reach the holy feet; 1275 asks for the light above the root centre and the steady gem-light in the middle path.
Both set a list of kin against Death's coming: 1266 with Death's rope and a household quarrelling over property, 1267 with Yama on the buffalo and a grief for kin called illusory.
Two vows rather than pleas: 1255 will speak only of the feet whether king or poor, 1276 will not forget them even in the deluded embrace of women.
Both akam laments end with a request for the hero's flowers, his garland in 1254 and kura blossoms in 1268, against Kama's arrows and the sea.

source_issues: 1262: line 274 (ஆக நகம்பட ஆர முயங்கிய) has no beat marker and may have lost words.
1269: மிகுமுனருபதானம் and நடைபெறு க்டுர are garbled.
1276: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ யர்தலங், உ லகமும்).
